lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Hello, I know you are worried about your baby. Bronchiolitis is a common lower respiratory tract infection in infants, which just means an infection in the small airways of the lungs.
lines.text_vi: Viêm tiểu phế quản là một nhiễm trùng đường hô hấp dưới phổ biến ở trẻ sơ sinh.
lines.source_quote: Bronchiolitis is a common lower respiratory tract infection in infants

lines.speaker: Parent
lines.text: Yes, she has been coughing, breathing fast, and having a hard time feeding for a few days now after a runny nose.
lines.text_vi: Vâng, con bé đã ho, thở nhanh và khó bú vài ngày nay sau khi bị sổ mũi.
lines.source_quote: Caregivers usually report a few days of coryza followed by cough, fast breathing, and feeding difficulty.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: That is very typical for this condition. We use supportive care as the main treatment, which includes keeping her hydrated, using nasal saline drops with gentle suctioning, and watching her breathing.
lines.text_vi: Chăm sóc nâng đỡ là phương pháp chính: bù nước, nhỏ nước muối sinh lý và hút mũi, theo dõi công thở.
lines.source_quote: Supportive care is the mainstay: hydration, nasal saline and suctioning, and monitoring work of breathing.

lines.speaker: Parent
lines.text: Do we need any special medicines or an X-ray?
lines.text_vi: Liệu chúng tôi có cần thuốc đặc biệt hay chụp X-quang không?
lines.source_quote: Diagnosis is clinical; routine chest radiography and laboratory tests are not required for uncomplicated cases.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: No, antibiotics and regular chest medicines do not routinely help with this type of viral infection. The illness usually lasts for several days, but please watch for worsening distress and come back immediately if she has trouble breathing or cannot feed.
lines.text_vi: Bố mẹ nên được tư vấn về diễn biến bệnh kéo dài vài ngày và khi nào cần đi khám gấp nếu bé mệt hơn.
lines.source_quote: Parents should be advised about expected illness course of several days and when to seek urgent review for worsening distress.
